title: Hermitian Monoids For Self-Dual Endo-Classes
body_html:
Hermitian Monoids For Self-Dual Endo-Classes

Fix a sign $\varepsilon$ and an extension $F/F_0$ of degree at most $2$.

For a self-dual extension $(E,\beta)$ of $F/F_0$, let

$$ \operatorname{herm}_{\varepsilon}(E/E_0) $$

be the monoid of isometry classes of $\varepsilon$-Hermitian spaces over $E/E_0$. It maps to the monoid of $E$-vector spaces by forgetting the Hermitian form.

For nonzero self-dual simple elements $\beta,\beta'$, the draft uses a unique bijection

$$ \mathfrak w_{\varepsilon,\beta',\beta}: \operatorname{herm}_{\varepsilon}(E/E_0) \to \operatorname{herm}_{\varepsilon}(E'/E'_0) $$

which preserves dimension and anisotropic dimension and satisfies

$$ \mathfrak w_{-1,\beta',\beta}(E(\beta))=E'(\beta'), \qquad \mathfrak w_{1,\beta',\beta}(E(\beta^2))=E'(\beta'^2). $$

For $\beta=\beta'=0$, the draft defines $\mathfrak w_{\varepsilon,0,0}$ to be the identity on $\operatorname{herm}_{\varepsilon}(F/F_0)$.

For a self-dual endo-class $\mathfrak c$, define $\operatorname{herm}_{\varepsilon}(\mathfrak c)$ as equivalence classes $[\beta,V]$, where $\beta$ is a self-dual simple element supporting a ps-character in $\mathfrak c$ and $V\in\operatorname{herm}_{\varepsilon}(F[\beta]/F[\beta]_0)$, modulo the identifications $\mathfrak w_{\varepsilon,\beta',\beta}$ for similar self-dual extensions.

For a non-self-dual endo-class $\mathfrak c$, the draft sets

$$ \operatorname{herm}_{\varepsilon}(\mathfrak c) = \operatorname{vect}(\mathfrak c). $$

Draft Caution

The TeX leaves a TODO about transfer on monoids of Hermitian spaces and the quaternionic case. This node records the intended structure, not a verified classification theorem.
